title: Release Club
tagline: Release club is a meta-platform for music NFTs. With Release Club, you gain the benefits of a curated music NFT platform that you control with the NFT contracts that you create.
description:
We built a product for collective curation on the Ethereum blockchain, where collaborators can BYOC (bring their own smart contracts) and create their own unique music platforms. 

Inspired by personal experiences we’ve had in the web3 creator space where we couldn’t find ways to release bodies of work with a collective of artist friends without losing ownership of our minted tokens to a central entity.

With Release Club’s current version, you gain the benefits of a curated music NFT platform that you control, with the contracts that you create from Zora’s Creator toolkit. Our future goal is to open the path for any type of contract to be pushed onto the platform.

By creating a club, a group of artists can define their own platform, craft a unique identity, and reach their audience, together.

Our contracts  act as a simple registry to put your club on chain and to make it easily discoverable by indexing on-chain data. 

Our factory contract deploys your custom club contracts and emits an event that existing indexers [e.g Spindex, neume-network] can use to find every Release Club deployment on Ethereum. 

Not only does this allow your club to be easily discovered, but this is also what makes it possible for our UI to be entirely optional. Fork it and build your custom experience.
how_its_made:
Our contracts  act as a simple registry to put your club on chain and to make it easily discoverable by indexing on-chain data. 

Our factory contract deploys your custom club contracts and emits an event that existing indexers [e.g Spindex, neume-network] can use to find every Release Club deployment on Ethereum. 

Not only does this allow your club to be easily discovered, but this is also what makes it possible for our UI to be entirely optional. Fork it and build your custom experience.

We’ll be providing an alternative route to use our club contracts inside of a custom build.

Since the club data is entirely on-chain, users can fork it and modify it to point at their deployed club contract and integrate it into their own user interface.
